summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA opens a multi-day deep dive into Alphabet after results that sent the stock down more than 10%. Revenue grew 25% to roughly a $500 billion annual run rate, but investors were spooked by negative free cash flow from booming AI spending and decelerating search growth. Query growth is the highest in five years, yet search revenue decelerated because users are searching more in AI Mode, which is still under-monetised — management is testing monetisation but has not ramped it to normal Google efficiency. The bright spot is Google Cloud, up 103%, which he presents as justification for nearly $200 billion of 2026 spending, alongside TPU chip demand from customers wanting a cheaper, price-performant alternative to Nvidia's dominant GPUs, and first-party model APIs processing 32 billion tokens a minute, up 40% quarter on quarter and over 4x year on year. The Gemini app has reached 1 billion users, the fastest-growing product in Google's history. Speaking as a shareholder since 2020, he is broadly comfortable with the spending but would like it moderated to match cash flow so the company need not dilute shareholders. No explicit buy, hold or sell rating and no fair value is stated in this part 1, so no call-event is recorded.
